title: Why the New Orleans bands stick together
summary: Russell and Penn discuss how loyalty and lack of arguments make Thomas's band play well together.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I mean that helps explain why you all play so well together too. I mean you all work together in every way and stick together. That's right. It's a good unit. A lot of bands aren't that way. They're fighting amongst themselves.

Mr. Bill, I've heard other musicians say when we be out together sometime that Thomas has got a bunch of men that never augurs, have no trouble on the bandstand like some bands usually do, and we don't.

Actually I think most of the New Orleans bands in the past and even today are the same type. They stick together nice, but you notice that more here than in other parts of the country. That's right. I notice it being all over the country at times. That's right. It's one of the characteristics of our music here that the bands play better together for some reason. Oh yeah. That may be one reason.

Well I think it is, Mr. Bill. I think it is. Because you know if you're playing in a band and you've got a bunch of men, nice men, playing with you and been playing with you for years and they never have an argument or nothing like that, well it's just a pleasure to be playing together. Everything goes along easy. But if you try to kick on one man all the time and probably that man is doing all right, maybe you just don't like something about him, I don't know, but that makes the band bad. You always have to get somebody hiring different men. We don't have no trouble like that.
